chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from one of his companions, raised it, saying:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ascended the pulpit in Kufa, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people, indeed sins are three,' then he paused.

Habbat al-Urani said to him, 'O Commander of the Faithful, you said sins are three, then you paused.' He said, 'I did not mention it except that I intended to explain it, but breathlessness presented itself to me, hindering between me and speech. Yes, sins are three: a sin that is forgiven, a sin that is not forgiven, and a sin for which we hope for its owner and fear for him.'

He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, explain them to us.' He said, 'Yes. As for the forgiven sin, it is a servant upon whom Allah punished for his sin in the world; for Allah is more forbearing and generous than to punish His servant twice.'

And as for the sin that is not forgiven, it is the injustices of the servants to one another. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He emerges to His creation, swears a vow upon Himself, saying: 'By My honor and majesty, the injustice of an unjust one will not pass Me by, even if it is a slap with a palm, or a touch with a palm, or a butting between the horned and the hornless.'
Thus, He will exact retribution for the servants from one another until no injustice remains for anyone against anyone. Then He will send them for reckoning.

And as for the third sin, it is a sin that Allah veiled over His creation and granted him repentance from it, so he became fearful of his sin, hoping for his Lord. So we are to him as he is to himself; we hope for him for mercy and fear for him the punishment.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of sins according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the tripartite nature of sins during a sermon in Kufa, distinguishing between sins expiated by worldly afflictions, those requiring divine retribution for interpersonal rights (Mazalim), and those veiled by Allah where the believer remains in a state of hope and fear. This classification underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the distinction between Allah's rights and the rights of creatures, particularly highlighting that interpersonal injustices are not automatically forgiven but require settlement between the parties or divine justice. The third category reflects the nuanced spiritual state of the faithful, balancing the fear of Allah's justice with the hope for His mercy regarding sins He has concealed.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad, from one of his companions, raising it, said,
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws ascended the Pulpit at Al-kufa, so heasws Praised Allahazwj and Extolled upon Himazwj, then said: ‘O you people! The sins are three (types)!’ Then heasws withheld.

So Habbat Al-Urany said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! You<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘The sins as three (types)’, then you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> withheld?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> did not mention it except that I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> intended to explain it, but breathlesness presented itself to me hindering between me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> and the speech. Yes, the sins are three – a Forgiven sin, and sin not Forgiven, and a sin its perpetrator hopes and fears upon’.

He said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! Explain these to us’. Heasws said: ‘Yes. As for the Forgiven sin, so a servant is Punished upon his sin by Allahazwj in the world, and Allahazwj is more Lenient and more Benevolent than Heazwj would be Punishing Hisazwj servant twice.

And as for the sin which is not Forgiven, so it is the injustices of the servants with each other. Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High, when He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Emerges to His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> creatures, would Vow with a Vow upon Himself<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> and He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Say: “And by My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My Majesty! No injustice of an unjust one would bypass Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and even if is it a slap by a slap, and even if it is touching by a palm, and even if it is a butting between the horned ones to the hornless ones”.

Thus, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will Retaliate for the servants from each other until there would not remain a single injusice for anyone upon anyone. Then He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Send them for the reckoning.

And as for the third (type of) sin, so it is a sin Veiled by Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> upon His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> creature, and Graces him the Turning (with Mercy) from Him<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>. Thus, he would wake up in the morning fearful from his sin, hoping to his Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>. So we<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> are to him just as he is to himself. We<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> are hoping for the Mercy for him, and we<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> are fearing for the Punishment upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad from certain individuals of his people in a marfu’ manner who has said the following:
“Once Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) climbed the Minbar (pulpit) in al-Kufah, praised Allah and spoke of His glory and then said, ‘O people sins are of three kinds’ and he remained quiet.

Habbah al-‘Arani, said, ‘O Amir al-Mu’minin, you just said, “Sins are of three kinds, and then remained silent.’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, I mentioned them and wanted to explain and inteipret them but a breathing problem prevented me from speaking. Yes, sins are of three kinds: A sin that is forgiven, a sin that is not forgiven and a sin for whose owner we have hopes and fears.’

The man said, ‘O Amir al-Mu’minin, explain them for us.’ “The Imam said, ‘Yes, the sin that is forgiven is one for which Allah has punished the sinner in this world and He is by far much Forbearing and Honorable to punish His servant twice.

“The sin that is not forgiven is people’s injustice to each other (in the matters of property and so forth). When Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, will manifest himself to His creatures, He will swear by His Ownself saying, ‘By My Majesty and Glory that the injustice of the unjust cannot bypass Me, even though it is in the form of a slap for a slap, a nibbing for a slap, or blow by those having horns to those without horns.’
He will retaliate for His servants from the others until no one will be left without receiving justice and thereafter they will be sent for reckoning.

“The third kind of sin is the sin that Allah has covered for His servants and has granted them repentance. He lives in fear because of his sin with hopes in his Lord. We toward him are just as he is to himself. We wish he will be granted mercy and fear for his suffering punishment.’”
